captions: To invest in stocks, mutual funds, or F&O,
the first step is a broker app.
But with so many apps, which one is best?
In this video — the major brokers' commissions, their apps,
the issues users have faced recently,
and which app is best for what — we'll cover it all.
One important note — this is not a promotion for any broker,
and not investment advice.
Charges change often —
check the current rates in the app before you choose.
First, the major brokers, their users, and their charges.
First — Groww.
Now the country's number one,
with one point three crore users.
The simplest app.
But one difference —
it charges twenty rupees on delivery; the other brokers give this free.
Its AMC is zero.
Second — Zerodha.
Seventy-nine and a half lakh users.
Delivery is free, F&O is twenty rupees, AMC three hundred.
It has a strong ecosystem — Kite, Coin, and Varsity.
Third — Angel One.
Seventy-six point four lakh users.
Delivery free, AMC two hundred forty.
Known for strong research reports.
Fourth — Dhan.
A new-age broker.
Delivery free, AMC zero.
Currently the number one app for options traders.
Upstox and Fyers are also good options for F&O.
Now the apps — where each one is strongest.
Zerodha — Kite is a pro trading platform,
Coin has over two thousand direct mutual funds,
and a single XIRR view across funds and stocks.
Varsity is free education, Sensibull is for options analysis.
Everything in one place.
Groww — the simplest app.
For mutual funds you don't even need a demat account,
just KYC.
Best for beginners.
But experienced traders find the features limited.
Dhan — TradingView charts, option chain, strategy tools,
and great speed.
An app built specifically for F&O and options traders.
Angel One — strong research reports and smart suggestions.
But some users complain about heavy notifications and promotions.
Now the important part —
the issues users have faced recently.
The biggest — on December fifth, twenty twenty-five,
a global service called Cloudflare went down, and Zerodha,
Angel One, Upstox, and Groww —
all the apps stopped working for about twelve minutes.
Logins and orders were stuck.
But this was no broker's fault — it was a third-party issue.
Zerodha — in the past,
Kite would slow down on expiry and high-volume days.
It's much improved now, and they've added a WhatsApp backup.
Groww —
it charges twenty rupees on delivery that other brokers give for free.
There are occasional complaints about charges and statements.
Angel One —
automatically closing intraday positions at three fifteen,
and heavy notifications — these draw complaints.
One reassurance — all these brokers are SEBI-registered.
Your shares are not with the broker; they're safe in your name at NSDL and CDSL.
Now the real question — which app is best for what?
Let's go by need.
For mutual funds — Groww is best.
Simple, no cost, and you don't even need a demat.
If you also trade, then Zerodha Coin,
because funds and stocks sit in one place.
For stocks and delivery — Zerodha or Dhan.
Free delivery, good tools, low AMC.
If you do large delivery volumes, Groww becomes a bit costly.
For futures and options — Dhan.
With its speed and TradingView charts,
it's number one for options.
Or Zerodha — with Kite, Sensibull, and reliability.
If you want everything in one place — Zerodha,
the best all-rounder with a full ecosystem.
Dhan is a modern, fast alternative.
So how do you choose a broker?
Five rules.
One — first, define your need.
Only mutual funds, or stocks, or F&O too?
Two — don't look at just the F&O rate.
Add up the total cost, including AMC and delivery charges.
Three — charges change often.
Verify the current rates in the app before you choose.
Four — all these brokers are SEBI-registered.
Your shares are safe at NSDL and CDSL.
Five — this is not a promotion for any broker,
and not advice.
The best one is simply the one that fits your need.
Brokers, at a glance.
Groww — simple, great for mutual funds and beginners.
But delivery is a bit costly.
Zerodha — the best all-rounder.
Strong ecosystem, education, and F&O.
Dhan — a fast app for F&O and options, with zero AMC.
Angel One — for research; Upstox and Fyers —
for active and algo traders.
No app is best for everyone —
the one that fits your need is best for you.
And verify the charges.
This information is aggregated from public sources —
it's not a promotion for any broker,
and not investment advice.
Thanks for watching.
